findings.reason: The production formula uses target density f, but f or its target P is not an algorithm input. Step 4 also relies on a “supplied admissibility check” without defining that input or its semantics. Specify the target density and a sound/exact check for support and integrability, or make those conditions explicit preconditions.

Proof step 1.1 says the pilot has a finite outcome space, although the algorithm permits a general measure space. Replace this with the measurable finite-valued selector argument and state the conditional conclusion almost surely given the pilot sigma-algebra.

The nested-level definition permits an arbitrary measurable probability space, while the referenced Feynman–Kac/SIR setup requires standard Borel state spaces. Add the standard Borel condition on (Ω, F) to the algorithm’s inputs.

The TV comparison needs a common finite Feynman–Kac setup: the same initial law, state spaces, potentials, and horizon for both kernel sequences. Otherwise zero kernel discrepancies need not give equal normalizers. State these assumptions and the inherited AC/standard Borel conditions explicitly.

Proof step 2.1 claims the estimator’s second moment is asymptotic to E[Z_a²]/n based only on p_a²/E[Z_a²]→0; this treats n as fixed although the statement does not say so. The logarithmic-efficiency claim can instead follow from p_a² ≤ E[ p̂² ] ≤ p_a² + E[Z_a²], whose bounds have the same leading logarithm.
The remark says relative error divides by P(A_L)². Relative error divides by P(A_L); relative variance divides by its square.
